questions.q: What has Yahweh done for his land and for the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob?
questions.a: Yahweh has made his land prosperous again by bringing back the Israelites who were exiles.

questions.q: What has Yahweh done about the sins of his people?
questions.a: He has forgiven his people all their sins.

questions.q: What has Yahweh done with his wrath and burning anger?
questions.a: Yahweh stopped punishing his people and ceased being angry with them.

questions.q: What does the psalmist ask of God?
questions.a: He asks God to save his people, to stop being upset with them, and make them strong again.

questions.q: What will God’s people do if God revives them again?
questions.a: God’s people will rejoice in him.

questions.q: What is the psalmist asking God do for his people?
questions.a: He is asking Yahweh to treat them kindly as he promised and save them from their troubles.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say Yahweh will say to his people?
questions.a: Yahweh will say that he will make his people thrive if they are loyal to him and do not do foolish things anymore.

questions.q: What will happen when Yahweh’s salvation comes for those who deeply revere him?
questions.a: Yahweh will be gloriously present with them in their land.

questions.q: What will the people who revere Yahweh experience?
questions.a: God’s faithful kindness and truth as well as his righteousness and peace.

questions.q: What will happen on the earth and from heaven when people revere God?
questions.a: People on earth will be faithful to God, and he will act justly toward them from heaven.

questions.q: What will happen when Yahweh gives what is good?
questions.a: The land will give its produce.

questions.q: What will Yahweh do as he considers what to do?
questions.a: Righteousness walks before Yahweh so he will recognize what the right thing is to do and he will do that.

commentary.text: Prayers for the continuance of former mercies.

Verses 1–7 The sense of present afflictions should not do away the remembrance of former mercies. The favour of God is the fountain of happiness to nations, as well as to particular persons. When God forgives sin, he covers it; and when he covers the sin of his people, he covers it all. See what the pardon of sin is. In compassion to us, when Christ our Intercessor has stood before thee, thou hast turned away thine anger. When we are reconciled to God, then, and not till then, we may expect the comfort of his being reconciled to us. He shows mercy to those to whom he grants salvation; for salvation is of mere mercy. The Lord's people may expect sharp and tedious afflictions when they commit sin; but when they return to him with humble prayer, he will make them again to rejoice in him.

Sooner or later, God will speak peace to his people. If he do not command outward peace, yet he will suggest inward peace; speaking to their hearts by his Spirit. Peace is spoken only to those who turn from sin. All sin is folly, especially backsliding; it is the greatest folly to return to sin. Surely God's salvation is nigh, whatever our difficulties and distresses are. Also, his honour is secured, that glory may dwell in our land. And the truth of the promises is shown by the Divine mercy in sending the Redeemer. The Divine justice is now satisfied by the great atonement. Christ, the way, truth, and life, sprang out of the earth when he took our nature upon him, and Divine justice looked upon him well pleased and satisfied. For his sake all good things, especially his Holy Spirit, are given to those who ask him. Through Christ, the pardoned sinner becomes fruitful in good works, and by looking to and trusting in the Saviour's righteousness, finds his feet set in the way of his steps. Righteousness is a sure guide, both in meeting God, and in following him
